conventions: אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה (7×: vv.2, 6, 10, 12, 22, 24, 25). The noun of אֲדֹנָי takes 'the Lord' with a supplied 'the' under rule 15, its 1cs suffix is unrepresented throughout because the ASV writes no possessive for it, and the name takes 'Jehovah'. Where the formula is the predicate of אֲנִי אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה (v.24), the construction-supplied copula joins the noun's unit under rule 20, giving 'am the Lord'. BSB represents the suffix; that is its documented convention and not evidence against this reading.

שׁוּט with the object marker (vv.24, 26). The same Hebrew is rendered two ways and the marker follows the ASV, not the lemma: 'that did despite unto them' gives 'unto' to the marker under rule 16, because the English verb reaches its object only through that word; 'those that do them despite' writes the object bare, so the marker is unrepresented and the suffix keeps 'them'. Do not level these two.

סָבִיב with מִן (vv.23, 24, 26). The adverbial expression — 'every side', 'round about' — is always סָבִיב's own rendering, headed on the word carrying its lexeme (rule 31); the מִן takes only whatever separate word the ASV writes for it ('on' v.23, 'of' v.24) and is unrepresented where the ASV writes none (v.26). The pair is never fused, because the ASV spends a word on each wherever it spends one at all, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is unmet.

Supplied English relatives. Where the ASV supplies a relative that makes an articleless participle, adjective or noun into an English noun phrase or relative clause, it joins that word's own unit and is not added (vv.7, 8, 9, 18, 19 under rule 46, and v.24's מִכֹּל סְבִיבֹתָם → 'of any that are round about them', where 'that are' stays with the noun even though the antecedent 'any' is written for כֹּל). Where the Hebrew writes its own finite clause beside a written antecedent and only the subordinator is supplied, that word is added (v.3 'that', v.14 'so that'). The v.24 fold is the chapter's one debatable case: rule 46's recast-noun rider is stated for a headless clause, so the competing reading marking 'that are' added under rule 55 is defensible and was not taken.

Surplus English 'and'. A coordinator standing between two phrases the Hebrew merely juxtaposes is added (v.5's italic 'and' between the two בְּ phrases, no waw being present). But an 'and' internal to a fixed English rendering of a single Hebrew word stays inside that word's unit: הִתְהַלָּכְתָּ → 'walked up and down' (v.14) is one rendering of the Hithpael's iterative sense, so its 'and' is written inside a rendering rather than beside one and rule 14's closing sentence does not reach it. Count the clause's waws against the ASV's connectives before applying this, as v.5 does.
report: Read all 46 lemma groups in the candidate table and then the full verse dump end to end, since the table cannot see `added` units and a split in this chapter would hide there. No cross-verse split found: every candidate showing two treatments is licensed by the source or by the ASV.

The closest call is the object marker with שוט in vv.24 and 26, and it is not a split: 'did despite unto them' spends an English word on the object relation, which the marker takes under rule 16's first family, while 'do them despite' writes the object bare and leaves the marker unrepresented. Rule 16's subtraction test yields exactly that pair, and v.26's note already records the contrast.

Article treatments are consistent. הסכך takes the written relative in v.14 (rule 41) and is unrepresented in v.16, where 'O covering cherub' leaves neither a 'the' nor a relative to place. השאטים takes bare 'that' in v.24 because the סביבת suffix already writes 'them', and 'those that' in v.26 where no antecedent stands.

מן with סביב is uniform across vv.23, 24 and 26: 'round about' / 'every side' is always סביב's own rendering, and the מן takes only the separate word the ASV writes for it ('on' in v.23, 'of' in v.24) and nothing in v.26. Likewise ביום/מיום plus infinitive in vv.13 and 15 both follow rule 52's closing clause, and both differ from the bare ב plus infinitive of vv.22 and 26 for the reason that rule gives.

Added-unit audit: four added units (v.3 'that', v.5 'and', v.10 'it', v.14 'so that'), each surviving the counts rules 14, 42 and 55 prescribe; I checked waw against connective in every verse and found no other surplus. The one deliberate non-count is v.14's 'walked up and down', whose internal 'and' stays inside the verb's unit, since rule 14 bars folding a coordinator written beside a rendering and this one is written inside one.

BSB: all 16 disagreements fall into documented convention classes — rule 27's lamed of לאמר, rule 40's recast prepositions (vv.4, 17, 26), rule 32's paragogic he at v.15, rule 22's resumptive suffix at v.25, the v.16 article, and the 1cs suffix of אדני in seven verses. None is a genuine error, and none should be changed to move the aggregate.

Residual, not patched: v.24 s015 folds 'that are' into סביבתם citing rule 46's recast-noun rider, but that rider sits inside rule 46's headless-relative paragraph and the antecedent here is written (כל → 'any'), so a competing added reading under rule 55 remains defensible and rule 8 wanted it named in the note. The edge itself is right, so I recorded the judgment as a convention rather than rewrite an accepted verse for a note alone, and did not promote it: one instance, no corpus behind it.
